column1: # THERE IS NO /bin/uname, AND ADDING ONE WOULD NOT WORK.  Recorded here because
# a symlink for it was added for RUNSHEET K5 and then removed, and neither step
# wrote down why -- notes/kernel-build.md sec 9 still carries the fossil, a
# sentence that says both "there is no symlink of mine left" and "it is declared
# as mine".  量 2026-08-29, this unit's own busybox under qemu-mips-static:
# `busybox uname -a` -> `uname: applet not found`.  The binary lists 50 applets
# and uname is not one of them, so the symlink would have exec'd busybox as
# `uname` and busybox would have refused.  K5 reads /proc/version instead, which
# prints linux_banner verbatim and therefore carries (user@host) and the gcc
# version that `uname -a` drops.  notes/kernel-build.md sec 12.7.
# /bin/dmesg was here, tagged `unit`, until 2026-08-28, and the adversarial pass
# found it. It is NOT in this unit's dump -- the dump has 50 busybox symlinks and
# that is not one of them -- and the byte string `dmesg` does not appear in this
# busybox at all, so the applet is not compiled in either. It was removed rather
# than retagged: an entry that adds nothing and was wrong about its own
# provenance is not worth a line. It got in because the `unit` tag was checked
# for `file` entries only, and 15 of the 31 entries were `slink`.
slink
slink
# --- one symlink that is MINE, and the reason it has to be ---
# /bin/uname was here too, and the adversarial pass killed it with the same
# instrument that killed /bin/dmesg. The note said "the applet IS in the binary
# (量: the string is present)" -- that was a `strings` FALSE POSITIVE, and
# `notes/rootfs-census.md` already documents the mirror of it. 量: busybox's
# applet-name table is at file offset 266740 and holds exactly 50 names, which are
# exactly the 50 symlinks in the dump; `uname` is not among them. The single
# `uname` hit in the file is at offset 9040, between `unsetenv` and `getpagesize`

# the build stamp can be read at all -- that is R3-6's to settle.
# --- without this, init runs with no stdio and it reads exactly like a hang ---

column1: # --- R3-9's second path to the flash: TWO read-only char nodes ---------------
# 🔄 2026-08-30, the rebuild. This block replaced a single `nod /dev/mtdblock1`
# row. That row was the best answer available WHILE CONFIG_MTD_CHAR WAS OFF, and
# the rebuild turned it on, so the row is withdrawn rather than corrected. The
# original reasoning is kept in notes/kernel-build.md 17.7a, which is where it
# was made.
# 讀 drivers/mtd/mtdchar.c mtd_open -- TWO refusals, and only the second depends
# on anything being configured right:
#   (a) if ((f_mode & FMODE_WRITE) && (minor & 1)) return -EACCES;
#   (b) if ((f_mode & FMODE_WRITE) && !(mtd->flags & MTD_WRITEABLE)) return -EACCES;
# (a) is unconditional and is stronger than a mode bit, because root ignores DAC.
# 讀 include/linux/mtd/mtd.h:21, MTD_CHAR_MAJOR is 90; the char minor is
# (mtd number << 1) and an ODD minor is the read-only alias. So mtd0ro = c 90 1
# and mtd1ro = c 90 3.
# WHY mtdblock1 IS GONE. Its stated purchase was "a readability and size reading
# through my own MTD stack" -- `wc -c` printing 2949120. /dev/mtd1ro buys the
# same number over the same partition through mtd_read -> part_read ->
# rtl819x_flash, and leaves NO WRITABLE FLASH NODE IN THE IMAGE AT ALL. What is
# given up is the block layer (mtdblock_readsect, the blktrans request queue),
# which no step of R3 exercises and which R5b will want; it comes back in the
# build that needs it.
# 🟢 AND THE CONTROL IS NOW COMPLETE RATHER THAN ARGUED. 17.7a's sentence was
# "the control is the absence of a node, not the mode bits", and an absence is
# only a control if nothing can create one. 量, notes/rootfs-census.md: `mknod`
# is NOT among this busybox's fifty applets -- by the applet-name table in the
# binary, not by `strings`, which is the false positive that file documents
# twice. So the declared set is the complete set of device nodes this image can
# ever hold, and a mistyped `/dev/mtd0` at the shell is `No such file or
# directory` rather than a writable handle on the loader.
# PREDICTIONS for the next seating, written now so the card copies rather than
# invents (notes/kernel-build.md 18.4 owns them):
#   cat /proc/mtd        -> 0x00130000 "boot+cfg+linux", 0x002d0000 "root fs",
#                           and it reads ZERO flash bytes
#   busybox wc -lc < /dev/mtd0ro -> `    4422   1245184`   (0x130000)
#     🔄 2026-08-31: `wc` is an APPLET and not a declared symlink here, so the
#     bare form returns `/bin/sh: wc: not found`. Measured on the silicon.
#     `-lc` and not `-c`: a byte count cannot see a truncating copy_from.
#   wc -c < /dev/mtd1ro  -> 2949120     (0x2D0000; 量 L3.log:114, and 讀
#                           rtl819x_flash.c: WINDOW_SIZE 0x400000 minus
#                           CONFIG_RTL_ROOT_IMAGE_OFFSET 0x130000. Two sources,
#                           because the first draft of the old row said 2818048,
#                           which is 0x2B0000 and a subtraction error)
#   echo x > /dev/mtd0ro -> `Permission denied`  <- the positive control on the
#                           safety property itself. It costs no flash bytes: the
#                           open fails before any write is issued. A SUCCESS
#                           here is a stop-if for the whole seating.
# 讀 mtd_read: `if (*ppos + count > mtd->size) count = mtd->size - *ppos;` then
# `if (!count) return 0;` -- a clean EOF, which is why `wc -c` terminates on a
# character device at all.
# NOT A CONTENT CHECK, and G8b's forbidden sentence stays forbidden. 量, two
# routes: this userspace has no dd/md5sum/od/hexdump/cmp/cksum/sum/sha1sum among
# its fifty applets, so nothing here reads a byte of H601 and compares it to
# anything. What these two nodes buy is size, readability, and a path over the
# forbidden region that is provably unable to write it.
nod

column1: # 🆕 2026-09-07 (`R5-5`): TWO MORE NODES, and the second one is the first
# chance this project has ever had to see refusal (b) fire.
# Refusal (a) -- the ODD-minor rule at mtdchar.c:73 -- is already exercised by
# `echo x > /dev/mtd0ro`.  Refusal (b) at :94, `!(mtd->flags & MTD_WRITEABLE)`,
# has NEVER fired on this board and cannot: every partition in this image comes
# from the vendor's map, which sets MTD_CAP_NORFLASH, so MTD_WRITEABLE is on and
# (b) is skipped.  rtl819x-spi registers with MTD_CAP_ROM -- flags 0 -- so
# /dev/mtd2, an EVEN minor, is the only path in this image where (b) is the
# thing that says no.
# 🔴 AND THE EVEN-MINOR NODE WAS REFUSED, BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN TOOL,
# BEFORE IT REACHED A BUILD.  `mkinitramfs.py` rejects any c:90:<even>:
#   "major 90 is mtdchar and minor 4 is EVEN ... only an ODD minor cannot be
#    opened for writing.  Declare /dev/mtd2ro as c:90:5 instead"
# That rule encodes refusal (a) alone, which is all it CAN check: whether
# (b) applies is a property of the driver's mtd->flags at run time, and a
# declaration file cannot see it.  🟢 The refusal is accepted rather than
# widened -- the guard it replaces was going to live in the CARD's shell
# command, and a guard in a command depends on the operator running the
# command as written, while a guard in the declaration does not.  So (b)
# stays 讀, verified in mtdchar.c:94 and never observed firing, and it is
# carried forward with its route: rtl819x-spi's `trywrite` verb reaches
# layer L2 on the silicon instead, which is the layer BEHIND (b).
# What the withdrawn node would have needed, kept because it is the argument
# the next attempt has to answer:  An even minor opened for writing is refused by (b) only if
# the device behind it is mine.  If `mtd2` were ever a vendor partition -- a
# third entry in rtl8196_parts1[], say -- the same `echo x > /dev/mtd2` would
# pass (a), pass (b), and attempt a REAL FLASH WRITE.  So the cell is written
#   grep -q 'rtl819x-spi-pio' /proc/mtd && echo x > /dev/mtd2
# and the shell does the checking.  讀 rtl819x_flash.c: with CONFIG_ROOTFS_SQUASH
# and no dual image, rtl8196_parts1[] has exactly TWO entries, so mtd2 is mine or
# nothing -- but "or nothing" is a prediction and this is the one place where a
# wrong prediction would be expensive rather than interesting.
# The minor arithmetic is the same as above: mtd2 = c 90 4, mtd2ro = c 90 5.
# Mode 0400 on both, so root's ignoring of DAC is what makes the refusal a
# KERNEL reading rather than a permission-bit one -- the same reasoning
# /dev/mtd0ro carries.
nod
column6: R5-5: read-only by the KERNEL (odd minor) over mtd2 = rtl819x-spi's own read-only device. `wc -c` must be 4194304, which is the SAME 4 MiB /dev/mtd0ro and /dev/mtd1ro cover between them but read through MY driver's programmed-I/O path instead of the vendor's. A size that is not 4194304 means add_mtd_device took a different index and every mtd2 cell on the card is void

column6: R5-6: the miscdevice rtl819x-wdt registers. 讀 include/linux/miscdevice.h:15 WATCHDOG_MINOR = 130, and MISC_MAJOR = 10 in the same file. 0600 because the only thing that opens it is a test run as root at the shell, and a mode that let any process arm the hardware watchdog on a one-device project is a wider door than the experiment needs. ⚠ OPENING THIS NODE ARMS THE SILICON: rtl819x_wdt_open() enters WDT_USER, and closing it WITHOUT writing 'V' first leaves the userspace deadline running, after which the board resets. That is the /dev/watchdog contract and not a defect, but it means `cat /dev/watchdog` is not a free read the way /dev/mtd0ro is, and no bench cell may treat it as one. The /proc/rtl819x-wdt verbs exist so that every experiment that does not specifically need the character device can avoid this node entirely.

column1: # R5-8, 2026-09-10.  Two entries, and the second is the only reason the keys
# driver ever polls.
# 讀 drivers/input/input-polldev.c: input-polldev queues its poll work from
# input_open_polled_device(), which is input_dev->open, which the input core
# calls when a HANDLER opens the device.  量 drivers/input/evdev.c:190 --
# evdev's input_open_device() is inside evdev_open(), gated on
# `!evdev->open++`, so it runs on the FIRST USERSPACE OPEN of the node and
# not at connect.  Without this node nothing in this image can perform that
# open, rtl819x-keys registers, /proc/rtl819x-keys appears, and every counter
# in it reads 0 for ever with CONFIG_PRINTK=n saying nothing about why.
# 🟢 THAT IS A CONTROL RATHER THAN A HAZARD, once the node exists.  n_open
# and n_poll then read
#     0 / 0            nothing has opened it
#     1 / rising       it is open and the workqueue is running
#     1 / flat         it was opened and closed
# which is the same three-state shape as R5-3a's line 25 being absent from
# /proc/interrupts before request_irq and after free_irq.  A bench cell opens
# it with `cat /dev/input/event0 > /dev/null &` and closes it by killing that.
# ⚠️ WHAT COMES OUT OF THE NODE IS BINARY AND NOTHING IN THIS IMAGE DECODES
# IT.  FW-46: this busybox has no dd, no md5sum and no --list, and nothing
# here has been shown to hold od or hexdump.  A `cat` of this node onto the
# console would put raw struct input_event bytes on the wire (16 bytes each
# on this 32-bit kernel, and ESC among them), which is why the cell above
# redirects to /dev/null: the OPEN is what is needed, not the data.  What the
# events were is read from /proc/rtl819x-keys' counters and its jiffies ring.
dir

column6: R5-8: evdev's node for the first registered input device, and the only way anything in this image can OPEN rtl819x-keys so that input-polldev starts polling. THE NUMBERS HAVE TWO SOURCES EACH, which is this project's rule for a constant entering code: major 13 is `#define INPUT_MAJOR 13` at include/linux/major.h:29 AND `13 char Input core` at Documentation/devices.txt:479; minor 64 is `#define EVDEV_MINOR_BASE 64` at drivers/input/evdev.c:11 AND drivers/input/Kconfig's own help for INPUT_EVDEV, *"char device 13:64+ - /dev/input/eventX"*. ⚠️ event0 AND NOT eventN: the minor is assigned by evdev in registration order, so this node is the first input device to register and nothing else in this image registers one -- REFUTED BY a /proc/bus/input/devices that lists more than one N: line, in which case the number this node names is a guess. 0600 for /dev/watchdog's reason: the only thing that opens it is a test run as root at the shell. 🟢 Unlike /dev/watchdog, OPENING THIS IS FREE -- it starts a poll loop and touches no register the vendor's own rtl_gpio_timer is not already reading once a second (量 FW-40).
